chunks: And whatever is narrated from Uthman ibn Ziyad, I have narrated it from Abd Al-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdus Al-Attar Al-Nisaburi, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaybah, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abd Al-Samad ibn Bashir, from Uthman ibn Ziyad.

key_terms.عَبْدُ الْوَاحِدِ: Abd Al-Wahid, a key narrator in the chain
key_terms.عُثْمَانَ بْنِ زِيَادٍ: Uthman ibn Ziyad, a prominent companion and narrator
key_terms.عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى: Uthman ibn Isa, a well-known narrator in Shia hadith

ai.seo_question: Who is the chain of narrators for the hadiths of Uthman ibn Ziyad?
ai.summary: This passage illustrates the meticulous methodology of Shaykh al-Saduq in verifying the reliability of Uthman ibn Ziyad, a key narrator often scrutinized for his role in the Battle of Karbala. By explicitly tracing the chain back to him, the text underscores the Shia scholarly principle of accepting individual narrators based on their specific trustworthiness (thiqa) rather than rejecting them outright due to historical context. This serves as a foundational example of how early Shia jurists constructed a robust corpus of hadith despite the political turbulence of the era.
